vocabulary.meaning_en: light, friendly conversation about easy topics like the weather
vocabulary.note_ar: يُستخدم في بداية الاجتماعات ونهايتها وفي المصعد
vocabulary.note_en: Used at the start and end of meetings, in lifts, etc.
vocabulary.example: We made small talk while we waited for the meeting to start.

vocabulary.meaning_en: talk to someone to find out what has happened since you last met
vocabulary.example: Let's meet for coffee and catch up.
I haven't seen my cousin for ages.

vocabulary.meaning_en: (weather) cold, grey and wet; very unpleasant
vocabulary.note_ar: يُقال أيضًا عن الشخص الحزين جدًا
vocabulary.note_en: Also used for a very unhappy person.
vocabulary.example: It's a miserable day; it hasn't stopped raining.

vocabulary.meaning_en: what you usually expect from a person, place or thing
vocabulary.note_ar: Typical! وحدها تعني: هذا متوقَّع كالعادة (غالبًا بتذمر)

vocabulary.meaning_en: the way your voice goes up and down when you speak
vocabulary.example: Your intonation goes up when you are happy about something.

vocabulary.meaning_en: even a very small amount of rain
vocabulary.note_ar: يُستخدم غالبًا في النفي: not a drop
vocabulary.note_en: Usually used in the negative: not a drop.
vocabulary.example: We haven't had a drop of rain for weeks.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a move to a higher position at work
vocabulary.example: She got a promotion last month.

vocabulary.meaning_en: finally do something or be in a situation
vocabulary.note_ar: يأتي بعده فعل بـ ing: end up getting
vocabulary.example: Did you end up buying the car?

vocabulary.meaning_en: from home or another place, not in the office
friendly greetings that you send to someone through another person
vocabulary.note_ar: give my regards to = أوصل تحياتي إلى
vocabulary.note_en: give my regards to = say hello to ... for me
vocabulary.example: Please give my regards to your parents.

vocabulary.note_en: Here it is friendly, not a criminal gang.
vocabulary.example: Say hello to the whole gang for me.
Everyone was very complimentary about her work.

vocabulary.note_ar: They really suit you = تليق بك حقًا

vocabulary.meaning_en: write a short message or email to someone
vocabulary.example: I'll drop you a line next week.
Give me a shout when you are free.
It's late; I'm going to head out.

vocabulary.meaning_en: take someone somewhere in your car
vocabulary.note_ar: في الأمريكية: give someone a ride
vocabulary.note_en: US English: give someone a ride.
vocabulary.example: Can I give you a lift to the station?

fine_lines.title: for ages vs in ages
fine_lines.explanation_ar: بعد I haven't seen you يمكن استخدام for أو in بنفس المعنى: منذ مدة طويلة. in أكثر شيوعًا في الإنجليزية الأمريكية.
fine_lines.explanation_en: After "I haven't seen you" you can use "for" or "in" with the same meaning. "In" is more common in American English.

examples.sentence: I haven't seen you for ages.
I haven't seen you in ages.

fine_lines.title: Rising vs falling intonation with "isn't it?"
fine_lines.explanation_ar: مع الطقس الجميل يرتفع الصوت بفرح، ومع الطقس السيّئ ينخفض الصوت. السؤال هنا لا ينتظر جوابًا حقيقيًا، بل يبدأ الحديث.
fine_lines.explanation_en: For nice weather your voice goes up happily; for bad weather it goes down. The question doesn't need a real answer; it starts a chat.

examples.sentence: Beautiful day, isn't it? Let's sit outside.
Miserable day, isn't it? I forgot my umbrella.

expressions.phrase: Hi, I'm ..., what brings you here?
expressions.meaning_ar: مرحبًا، أنا ...، ما الذي جاء بك إلى هنا؟
expressions.meaning_en: An informal way to ask why someone is at an event or meeting.
expressions.example: Hi, I'm Sara. What brings you here?

expressions.phrase: Is this your first time here?
expressions.meaning_ar: هل هذه أول مرة تأتي فيها إلى هنا؟
expressions.meaning_en: Asks if someone is new to the place or event; a good opener.
expressions.example: Hi, I'm Omar. Is this your first time here?

expressions.meaning_en: Asks the reason someone is at a place.
expressions.example: So what are you here for, the training course?

expressions.meaning_ar: زمان ما شفتك! / مضى وقت طويل لم أرك
expressions.meaning_en: An informal greeting when you meet someone after a long time.
expressions.example: Ali! Long time no see!

expressions.phrase: It's great to see you again.
expressions.meaning_en: A warm greeting for someone you know.
expressions.example: Hi, Peter. It's great to see you again.

expressions.phrase: I haven't seen you for ages / in ages.
expressions.meaning_en: Says it has been a long time since you met.
expressions.example: Hello! I haven't seen you in ages.

expressions.meaning_en: An informal way to ask about someone's life in general.
expressions.example: Hi, Mona. How are things?

expressions.meaning_en: A friendly comment about nice weather to start a chat.
expressions.example: Beautiful day, isn't it? So sunny!

expressions.meaning_en: A comment about bad weather to start a chat.
expressions.example: Miserable day, isn't it? Cold and wet.

expressions.meaning_en: Said when something bad happens that often happens.
expressions.example: It's raining on the weekend again. Typical!

expressions.phrase: It looks like it's going to rain / snow.
expressions.meaning_en: A prediction based on what you can see.
expressions.example: Look at those clouds. It looks like it's going to rain.

expressions.phrase: It wouldn't surprise me if it rains.
expressions.meaning_en: You think it is quite likely to rain.
expressions.example: Take a coat. It wouldn't surprise me if it rains.

expressions.phrase: We haven't had a drop of rain for weeks.
expressions.meaning_ar: لم تنزل قطرة مطر منذ أسابيع.
expressions.meaning_en: It has been completely dry for a long time.
expressions.example: The garden is so dry. We haven't had a drop of rain for weeks.

expressions.phrase: The last time I saw you, you were ...
expressions.meaning_en: Reminds someone of their news so they continue the story.
expressions.example: The last time I saw you, you were looking for a new job.

expressions.phrase: Did you end up getting that promotion?
expressions.meaning_ar: هل حصلت على تلك الترقية في النهاية؟
expressions.meaning_en: Asks about the result of a plan the person told you about.
expressions.example: Did you end up getting that promotion?

expressions.phrase: I remember you were planning to ...
expressions.meaning_en: Asks about a plan the person had.
expressions.example: I remember you were planning to start a business.

expressions.meaning_en: Introduces news about a person or thing.
expressions.example: Did you hear about the new manager?

expressions.phrase: You won't believe it when I tell you ...
expressions.meaning_en: Introduces surprising news.
expressions.example: You won't believe it when I tell you what happened.

expressions.meaning_en: Says you have exciting news to share.
expressions.example: Wait till I tell you about my trip!

expressions.meaning_en: Asks if someone has the same job as before.
expressions.example: Are you still working for the IT company?

expressions.meaning_en: Asks a student about their studies.
expressions.example: How are your studies going? What year are you in?

expressions.meaning_en: Asks generally about someone's job.
expressions.example: So, how's work going these days?

expressions.phrase: How do you like working remotely?
expressions.meaning_ar: ما رأيك في العمل عن بُعد؟
expressions.meaning_en: Asks someone's opinion of working from home.
expressions.example: How do you like working remotely? Do you miss the office?

expressions.meaning_en: Asks about someone's children.
expressions.example: How are the kids? Getting bigger, I'm sure.

expressions.meaning_en: Asks about another person you both know.
expressions.example: How is Adam doing?

expressions.phrase: Please say hi to ... for me.
expressions.meaning_en: Asks someone to pass on your hello.
expressions.example: Please say hi to your brother for me.

expressions.meaning_en: A more formal way to send your greetings.
expressions.example: Please give my regards to your family.

expressions.meaning_en: Starts a chat about someone you both know.
expressions.example: Have you seen Michael recently?

expressions.meaning_en: Asks if someone has had any contact or news from a person.
expressions.example: Have you heard from David? I think he's travelling.

expressions.meaning_en: A compliment about someone's new look.
expressions.example: Oh, I like your new hairstyle!

expressions.meaning_en: Something has had a very good effect.
expressions.example: That exercise plan has really worked wonders.

expressions.phrase: I really love those shoes. Where did you get them?
expressions.meaning_ar: أحب حذاءك كثيرًا. من أين اشتريته؟
expressions.meaning_en: A compliment plus a question to keep the chat going.
expressions.example: I really love those shoes. Where did you get them?

expressions.meaning_en: A simple, safe compliment.
expressions.example: Wow, you look great! It's good to see you.

expressions.meaning_en: Says something someone wears looks good on them.
expressions.example: You've got glasses! They really suit you.

expressions.phrase: Sorry, I've really got to go.
expressions.meaning_en: A polite way to leave a conversation.
expressions.example: Sorry, I've really got to go, but let's catch up soon.

expressions.phrase: Give me your number / email and I'll drop you a line.
expressions.meaning_ar: أعطني رقمك / بريدك وسأرسل لك رسالة.
expressions.meaning_en: Asks for contact details to stay in touch.
expressions.example: Give me your email and I'll drop you a line.

expressions.meaning_ar: من الأفضل أن أدعك تذهب (لا أريد أن أؤخرك).
expressions.meaning_en: A polite way to end a chat, as if you don't want to take more of their time.
expressions.example: I'd better let you go. I've taken up so much of your time.

expressions.phrase: It was really great talking to you.
expressions.meaning_en: A friendly way to end a conversation.
expressions.example: It was really great talking to you.

expressions.phrase: We must catch up again soon.
expressions.meaning_ar: يجب أن نلتقي ونتبادل الأخبار قريبًا.
expressions.meaning_en: Says you want to meet and talk again.
expressions.example: We must catch up again soon. Let's not wait so long.

expressions.meaning_en: Informal: contact me.
expressions.example: Give me a shout and we'll get together for coffee.

expressions.phrase: I'm really sorry, but I have to leave now.
expressions.meaning_ar: أنا آسف حقًا، لكن عليّ المغادرة الآن.
expressions.meaning_en: A polite way to say you must go.
expressions.example: I'm really sorry, but I have to leave now. I'll talk to you later.

expressions.phrase: It's time for me to head out.
expressions.meaning_en: Says you are leaving now.
expressions.example: It's time for me to head out. I have a train to catch.

expressions.phrase: Can I give you a lift?
expressions.meaning_en: Offers to drive someone somewhere.
expressions.example: It's raining. Can I give you a lift?

grammar.title: Question tags for small talk: ..., isn't it?
grammar.explanation_ar: نضيف isn't it? في نهاية جملة عن الطقس لنطلب موافقة الآخر ونبدأ الحديث. الجملة الأصلية مختصرة: (It's a) beautiful day, isn't it? الجملة موجبة فيكون السؤال المذيَّل منفيًا.
grammar.explanation_en: We add "isn't it?" to the end of a comment to ask for agreement and start a chat. "Beautiful day" is short for "It's a beautiful day". A positive sentence takes a negative tag.

grammar.title: end up + -ing
grammar.explanation_ar: end up تعني: في النهاية حصل كذا. بعدها نستخدم الفعل مع ing. نستخدمها لنسأل عن نتيجة خطة سمعنا عنها.
grammar.explanation_en: "End up" means "in the end". Use the -ing form after it. We use it to ask about the result of a plan.
examples: Did you end up getting that job?
We ended up staying at home.
Did you end up doing that trip?

grammar.title: Present perfect with for / in + time
grammar.explanation_ar: نستخدم المضارع التام المنفي مع for أو in لنقول إن شيئًا لم يحدث منذ مدة: haven't + التصريف الثالث.
grammar.explanation_en: Use the negative present perfect (haven't + past participle) with "for" or "in" to say something hasn't happened for a period of time.
examples: I haven't seen you for ages.
We haven't had rain in weeks.
She hasn't called me for a month.

questions.question: You meet a friend after two years. What do you say?
choices: Is this your first time here?
questions.explanation_ar: Long time no see تُقال عند لقاء شخص بعد مدة طويلة.
questions.explanation_en: "Long time no see" is for meeting someone after a long time.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
choices: I didn't see you for ages.
I haven't seen you for ages.
I haven't saw you in ages.
I don't see you in ages.
questions.explanation_en: We use the present perfect: haven't seen.

questions.question: "Miserable day, isn't it?" — what is the weather like?
questions.explanation_ar: miserable عن الطقس تعني باردًا ورطبًا وكئيبًا.
questions.explanation_en: Miserable weather is cold, grey and wet.

questions.question: Did you end up ___ that new job?
questions.explanation_ar: بعد end up نستخدم الفعل مع ing.
questions.explanation_en: After "end up" we use the -ing form.

questions.question: What does "Please give my regards to your family" mean?
choices: Please say hello to your family for me.
Please give your family a present.
questions.explanation_ar: give my regards to تعني: أوصل تحياتي.
questions.explanation_en: It means "say hello to them for me".

questions.question: Which phrase is a polite way to END a conversation?
questions.explanation_ar: I'd better let you go عبارة مهذبة لإنهاء الحديث.
questions.explanation_en: "I'd better let you go" ends a chat politely.

questions.question: "Can I give you a lift?" means:
choices: Can I help you carry this?
Can I take you up in the elevator?
Can I give you a present?
questions.explanation_ar: give someone a lift = يوصل شخصًا بسيارته.
questions.explanation_en: "Give someone a lift" means drive them somewhere.

questions.question: Look at those dark clouds. It looks like it's going ___ rain.
questions.explanation_ar: going to + الفعل للتنبؤ بما نراه.
questions.explanation_en: "Going to + verb" for a prediction based on what we see.

questions.question: Which is a good compliment?
choices: Those glasses really suit for you.
questions.explanation_ar: suit فعل متعدٍّ بلا حرف جر، وglasses جمع فلا نضيف s.
questions.explanation_en: "Suit" takes no preposition, and "glasses" is plural, so "suit" has no -s.

questions.question: "Give me a shout" means:
questions.explanation_ar: Give me a shout عبارة غير رسمية تعني: اتصل بي.
questions.explanation_en: "Give me a shout" is informal for "contact me".
